scope: Full-region numeric coverage and comparison against the human recording; not a visual acceptance or renderer fix

human_comparison.limitations: Lower-body/player samples differ more, up to 0.3177 in a median channel. The entire simulation and vehicle pose are not identical; these distributions are not time-aligned.

findings: Two runs each inspect every one of 162304 texels in x=[518,1152), y=[64,320) for 300 frames after gamma/FXAA. No sampled texel is near black by the stated threshold.
In the right subregion x=[756,1073), y=[128,256), the greatest isolated max-channel dip is 10/1023, with zero >30% / >51/1023 fall or pulse events. The larger changes occur farther left.

The earlier changing point (720,193) cannot by itself establish the cause of the human-circled right-hand flash. Its target albedo and static draws sometimes change the pixel and sometimes leave it unchanged. Position-producing vertex constants and reflected albedo constants/sampler descriptors are stable across run 06. Preceding draw/depth/texture contents remain unmeasured.

The new pre-host full-frame 144-point grid matches the original human recording coordinates exactly. Ten upper-right point distributions have overlapping RGB ranges and at most 12/1023 median-channel difference. This supports similar scene output at those points, not full visual equivalence.
limitations: Only the native guest-output resource after host gamma/FXAA is covered. The presenter scaling/sharpening and swapchain image have not yet been measured.
All texels contribute within the reported region, but this does not prove the initial human-circled feature has exactly the same pixel bounds in this later saved view.
The probe adds GPU readback and CPU aggregation work and may change timing. This is not a performance benchmark.
The original human confirmed flicker, but that recording only contains sparse pre-host samples. No negative claim about the human observation follows from these private runs.
Remaining billboard readability, outdoor rain visibility, final performance acceptance and final LIVE promotion remain unresolved.
next_step: Trace numeric region statistics on the application-owned swapchain back buffer after native presenter effects, using the existing paint submission fence; inspect session/presentation differences if the symptom remains absent. Do not use desktop capture or modify render behavior speculatively.
